body.p: Claims 1-10 are pending in the application. New Claims 11 and 12 have been presented for the Examiner's consideration. Reconsideration of the rejections set forth in the aforementioned Final Office Action is respectfully requested in view of the above amended and new claims, and following remarks. The basis for these amended and new claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed.

Applicant respectfully submits that the above amended and new claims overcome the current rejections of record and, as such, all the claims are now in condition for allowance. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests completion of prosecution and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. However, should the Examiner elect to issue an Office Action in response to this Amendment After Final, Applicant hereby requests a telephonic interview with the Examiner prior to issuance of any Office Action in order to discuss any remaining issues.

As previously stated, Applicant respectfully acknowledges the Examiner's interpretation of Claims 4, 5, 7 and 8 in the Office Action. However, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner's interpretation in this regard may too narrowly define Applicant's noted claim terms and that Applicant's noted claim terms could be characterized more broadly. As such, Applicant does not acquiesce that the noted claim terms are to be interpreted as solely, exactly expressed by the Examiner.

Claims 1-8 and 10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Additionally/alternatively, Claims 4, 5 and 7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451 and further in view of Yasuda et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0278278. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Poeppel et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2023/0205202 in view of Wilson et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0361451 and further in view of Christen et al., U.S. Patent Application Publication No. US 2019/0219411. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Examiner's characterization that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, renders Applicant's claimed disclosure obvious. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. It is respectfully submitted that Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, teaches away from Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle

control system and vehicle control device. Applicant's claimed disclosure recites an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device having a unique and advantageous orientation and combination of components which are more efficient, advantageous, and eliminate various negative features associated with the devices/systems disclosed in the cited references.

Applicant's claimed disclosure is directed toward an improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device which are capable of maintaining safety and appropriately providing relief to a failed autonomous driving vehicle. Applicant's improved vehicle control system and vehicle control device are able to accomplish these tasks as a result of their unique and advantageous arrangement and orientation of components and features which include, in part, the following:

a center device including at least one processor and a memory coupled to the at least one processor, configured to acquire a type of a passenger of an autonomous driving vehicle, the type of the passenger being stored in the memory of the center device before starting autonomous driving of the autonomous driving vehicle; and

a second stop position is a nearest position to a present position of the autonomous driving vehicle and selected from a rest area, a parking area, a parking lot of a public facility, a bus stop, an emergency parking zone, and a road shoulder having a width equal to or greater than a width of the vehicle.

Specifically in this regard, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 set forth Applicant's unique and innovative arrangement and orientation of components, reciting a vehicle control system and a vehicle control device, respectively, including, in part, "the center device includes at least one processor and a memory coupled to the at least one

processor, configured to . .. acquire a type of a passenger of the autonomous driving vehicle, the type of the passenger being stored in the memory of the center device before starting autonomous driving of the autonomous driving vehicle" and "the second stop position being a nearest position to a present position of the autonomous driving vehicle and selected from a rest area, a parking area, a parking lot of a public facility, a bus stop, an emergency parking zone, and a road shoulder having a width equal to or greater than a width of the vehicle." Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest, at least, any structure similar to a vehicle control system and a vehicle control device including, in part, "the center device includes at least one processor and a memory coupled to the at least one processor, configured to ... acquire a type of a passenger of the autonomous driving vehicle, the type of the passenger being stored in the memory of the center device before starting autonomous driving of the autonomous driving vehicle" and "the second stop position being a nearest position to a present position of the autonomous driving vehicle and selected from a rest area, a parking area, a parking lot of a public facility, a bus stop, an emergency parking zone, and a road shoulder having a width equal to or greater than a width of the vehicle" as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure. There is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. In fact, the cited references teach away from and articulate various disadvantages associated with the arrangement, configuration and orientation of components taught in Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Regarding a type of a passenger, Poeppel et al. describes systems and methods for remote status detection of autonomous vehicles. While Wilson et al. describes a system and method for rendezvous coordination of an autonomous automotive vehicle with an ambulance.
Poeppel et al. discloses a human-machine interface system 118 placed in a vehicle computing system 102.
First, the human-machine interface system 118 is placed in a vehicle 104 because "the vehicle 104 incorporates the vehicle computing system 102."

Second, the human-machine interface system 118 can include one or more input device(s) (e.g., touchscreens, keypad, touchpad, knobs, buttons, sliders, switches, mouse, gyroscope, microphone, other hardware interfaces) configured to receive user input.

That is, the human-machine interface system 118 is not placed in a center device. In addition, the human-machine interface system 118 does not acquire a type of a passenger, the type of the passenger being stored in a memory of the center device before starting autonomous driving of an autonomous driving vehicle as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure.
Regarding a second stop position, the amended claims clarify the second stop position.
Poeppel et al. discloses "a designated parking location or emergency shoulder."
Poeppel et al. does not describe, disclose, teach or suggest a selection from a rest area, a parking area, a parking lot of a public facility, a bus stop, an emergency parking
zone, and a road shoulder having a width equal to or greater than a width of the vehicle as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6 of Applicant's claimed disclosure.

Thus, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, does not disclose, teach or suggest Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device as recited in amended independent Claims 1 and 6, respectively, of Applicant's claimed disclosure. The deficiencies found in Poeppel et al. are not corrected by the combination of Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited. Additionally, there is no motivation or incentive in Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, to arrive at Applicant's disclosure as claimed. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that amended independent Claims 1 and 6, and all claims depending directly or indirectly therefrom (Claims 2-5 and 7-10), are not obvious in light of and are patentable over Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's succinct arguments set forth above and previously, Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, fails to disclose, teach or suggest several features that are recited in Applicant's claimed disclosure. As such, Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and vehicle control device are not disclosed, taught or suggested by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited.

Without conceding to the correctness of the Examiner's comments thereto, Applicant respectfully submits that Claims 2-5 and 7-10 are allowable, at least, for the same reasons given above for amended independent Claims 1 and 6, because Claims 2-5 and 7-10 are ultimately dependent on either amended independent Claim 1 or amended independent Claim 6.

It is respectfully submitted that in view of Applicant's arguments stated above and previously, Poeppel et al. is an improper primary reference, Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. are improper secondary references, and Applicant's claims are patentably distinct with respect thereto, as well as no teaching in existence to suggest the combination of any of the cited references. As set forth in MPEP § 2142, "the key to supporting any rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 is the clear articulation of the reason(s) why the claimed invention would have been obvious." As the U.S. Supreme Court noted in KSR Intl. Co. v. Teleflex Inc., "the analysis supporting a rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 should be made explicit." 82 USPQ2d 1385, 1396 (2007). The Federal Circuit has stated that "rejections on obviousness cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness." In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977 at 988, 78 USPQ2d 1329 at 1336 (Fed. Cir. 2006). In the Final Office Action, the Examiner's conclusory statements are insufficient to establish a prima facie rejection because no articulated reasoning with rational underpinning was given, and no explanation as to exactly how the combination or modification could have been made was provided. As a result, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner has failed to
identify any motivation by one of ordinary skill in the art to combine or modify the art to arrive at the claimed disclosure other than the impermissible use of hindsight.

While it is Applicant's view that the claims as written are not obvious in light of the cited art and fully comply with Section 103, in the interest of advancing and expediting prosecution, and without prejudice to pursuing this and related subject matter in future applications, Applicant has amended independent Claims 1 and 6. Therefore, amended independent Claims 1 and 6 should be in condition for allowance. Further, because Claims 2-5 and 7-10 depend from either amended independent Claim 1 or amended independent Claim 6, directly or indirectly, they are at least as limited, are similarly not taught by Poeppel et al., alone or in combination with Wilson et al., Yasuda et al. and Christen et al. or any of the other references cited, and should also be in condition for allowance. In view of the above amendments and these remarks, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider and withdraw the Section 103 rejections to Claims 1-10 .

New Claims 11 and 12 have been presented for the Examiner's consideration. Support for these new claims can be found throughout the specification, claims and drawings as originally filed. No new matter has been added. It is respectfully submitted that new dependent Claims 11 and 12 further help to define Applicant's unique and innovative vehicle control system and its structural differences over the cited references.

Accordingly, in view of these remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that new Claims 11 and 12 are in condition for allowance. As such, Applicant respectfully requests favorable consideration of new Claims 11 and 12.

All of the stated grounds of rejection have been properly traversed, accommodated or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests the Examiner to reconsider all presently outstanding rejections and that they be withdrawn. It is believed that a full and complete response has been made to the outstanding Final Office Action and, as such, the present application is in condition for allowance. Thus, prompt and favorable consideration of this Amendment After Final is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes that personal communication will expedite prosecution of this application, they are invited to contact the undersigned at their earliest convenience.
